rot.pin.ideia.ex1.e1: Attack: in 1858, at the Paris Opera, Paul Morphy played White against the Duke of Brunswick and Count Isouard, who played together. The black king is still on e8.
rot.pin.ideia.ex1.e2: When a piece stands between the attacker and the king, it cannot leave the line: the rules do not allow the king to be left in check. Such a piece is pinned, and this is an absolute pin. See it next.
rot.pin.ideia.ex1.p: Two white pieces attack the pawn on b5. Find the best move.
rot.pin.ideia.ex1.certo: The bishop captures the pawn with check. Whatever black piece steps onto d7 will stand between the bishop and the king.
rot.pin.ideia.ex1.revela: The right capture is with the bishop, with check: whatever black piece steps onto d7 will be stuck in front of the king.
rot.pin.ideia.ex1.err.b3b5.1: The queen captures the pawn on b5 with check.
rot.pin.ideia.ex1.err.b3b5.2: With this move Black has a resource: the black queen steps onto d7, defended, and offers the exchange of queens.
rot.pin.ideia.ex1.err.b3b5.3: Back to the position: look for the capture that leaves a black piece stuck in front of the king.
rot.pin.ideia.ex1.err.g5f6.1: The bishop captures the knight on f6.
rot.pin.ideia.ex1.err.g5f6.2: With this move Black has a resource: the queen gives check on b4 and offers the exchange of queens.
rot.pin.ideia.ex1.err.g5f6.3: Back to the position: look for the capture with check on b5.
rot.pin.ideia.ex1.fora: That move does not capture the pawn on b5. Look for the capture with check.
rot.pin.ideia.ex1.volta: Try again: look for the best capture on b5.
rot.pin.ideia.ex1.l0: Black is in check. The bishop on b5 is defended by the queen on b3, and Black chooses how to defend.
rot.pin.ideia.ex1.l1: Black puts the knight on d7, between the bishop and the king. Now it is pinned: it cannot leave d7, neither to capture nor to block another check, because that would leave the king in check.
rot.pin.ideia.ex1.l2: White castles queenside, and the rook reaches d1 to attack the pinned knight once more. It cannot run away: it can only be defended.
rot.pin.ideia.ex1.l3: In positions like this, the pinned piece cannot run, and it pays to attack it again with another piece. Morphy followed that plan and mated on move 17.
rot.pin.ideia.ex2.e1: Attack: this position comes from a game played on Lichess. The black pawn on b5 attacks your queen on a4 and your bishop on c4, and the pawn on a6 defends it.
rot.pin.ideia.ex2.e2: But the pawn on a6 stands between your queen and the rook on a8. It may move, and then the rook is exposed. This is a relative pin: the piece may move, but it pays dearly.
rot.pin.ideia.ex2.p: Your queen and your bishop are attacked by the pawn on b5. Find the best move.
rot.pin.ideia.ex2.certo: The bishop captures the pawn on b5. If the pawn on a6 recaptures, it leaves the a-file, and your queen captures the rook on a8.
rot.pin.ideia.ex2.revela: The move is to capture on b5 with the bishop: the pawn on a6 is pinned to the rook on a8, and recapturing costs the rook.
rot.pin.ideia.ex2.err.c3b5.1: The knight captures the pawn on b5, and your queen and bishop are out of the attack.
rot.pin.ideia.ex2.err.c3b5.2: With this move Black has a resource: the bishop leaves c8, and the queen on d8 now defends the rook on a8.
rot.pin.ideia.ex2.err.c3b5.3: Back to the position: the pawn on a6 is tied to the rook on a8. Look for the capture that uses this now.
rot.pin.ideia.ex2.err.a4b3.1: The queen retreats to b3 and defends the bishop on c4.
rot.pin.ideia.ex2.err.a4b3.2: With this move Black has a resource: the pawn captures the bishop on c4, and the queen only wins back a pawn.
rot.pin.ideia.ex2.err.a4b3.3: Back to the position: see what stands behind the pawn on a6 before retreating.
rot.pin.ideia.ex2.fora: That move leaves one of your pieces attacked by the pawn on b5. Look for the capture on b5.
rot.pin.ideia.ex2.volta: Try again: look for the capture on b5.
rot.pin.ideia.ex2.l0: Now the bishop on b5 attacks the knight on c6, and Black is a pawn down.
rot.pin.ideia.ex2.l1: Black recaptures anyway, so as not to stay a pawn down. The pawn leaves the a-file, and the rook on a8 is left unprotected.
rot.pin.ideia.ex2.l2: The queen captures the rook on a8. White gave up a bishop and won a rook and a pawn.
rot.pin.ideia.ex2.l3: In positions like this, with a bigger piece behind, a relative pin does not forbid the move, but it charges a high price. Before moving a piece, see what stands behind it.
rot.pin.demos.absoluta.1: Attack: now with Black, in a Slav Defence game played on Lichess. The white queen on c3 stands on the diagonal of the king on e1, and your queen on a5 watches that diagonal.
rot.pin.demos.absoluta.2: The bishop goes to b4 and pins the queen to the king. Capturing the bishop costs the queen, because your queen on a5 defends it.
rot.pin.demos.absoluta.3: White castles to take the king off the diagonal. The pin is gone, but the queen is still attacked, and it is Black to move.
rot.pin.demos.absoluta.4: The bishop captures the queen. White wins back only the bishop: Black wins the queen for a bishop.
rot.pin.demos.relativa.1: Attack: Black again, in a Caro-Kann game between titled players. The pawn on b4 attacks your queen and your bishop, and the pawn on a3 defends it.
rot.pin.demos.relativa.2: The bishop captures the pawn on b4. The pawn on a3 stands between your queen and the rook on a1: it is a relative pin.
rot.pin.demos.relativa.3: White wins the bishop back, but the pawn leaves the a-file.
rot.pin.demos.relativa.4: The queen captures the rook on a1. The pawn was allowed to move, and the price was the rook.
rot.pin.demos.excecao.1: Attack: in Paris, in 1750, Légal played White against Saint Brie. The bishop on g4 pins the knight on f3 to the queen on d1. The knight looks stuck.
rot.pin.demos.excecao.2: Even so, the knight leaves and captures the pawn on e5. The queen on d1 is left attacked by the bishop.
rot.pin.demos.excecao.3: Black captures the queen, which is the mistake: taking the knight back with the pawn on d6 only lost a pawn.
rot.pin.demos.excecao.4: The bishop captures on f7 with check. The knight on e5 defends it.
rot.pin.demos.excecao.5: The king steps out of check through the only square: e7.
rot.pin.demos.excecao.6: The other knight goes to d5 and gives mate. The relative pin did not hold the knight on f3, because the price of leaving was a mate.
rot.pin.demos.excecao.7: Back to the position: before trusting a relative pin, check what the pinned piece gains by leaving. The position decides whether it holds.
rot.pin.pratica.valeAqui.enunciado: Now you play Black. Your bishop on b7 pins the pawn on g2 to the king on h1. Is it worth capturing the pinned pawn? Play as Black and find the best move.
rot.pin.pratica.valeAqui.fim: On h3 the rook captured with check, and the pinned pawn on g2 could not recapture. The king went to g1, and the rook gave mate on h1.
rot.pin.pratica.valeAqui.err.b7g2: The bishop captures the pawn with check, but the king recaptures, and the pin is gone. Use the pin: the pawn on g2 cannot leave the diagonal.
rot.pin.pratica.valeAqui.err.h8g8: The rook attacks the pinned pawn once more, but without check, and White gains time to defend. Look for a move that the pinned pawn cannot answer.
rot.pin.pratica.pecaPresa.enunciado: Now with White. Look for an undefended black piece that you can pin to the king. Play as White and find the best move.
rot.pin.pratica.pecaPresa.fim: On d5 the bishop pinned the rook to the king. The king stepped to g7, but the rook was still attacked and undefended, and the bishop captured it.
rot.pin.pratica.pecaPresa.err.h4d8: The check drives the king from g8, and the rook on e6 is no longer on its line. Look for the black piece you can pin to the king.
rot.pin.pratica.pecaPresa.err.f3b7: The bishop captures the pawn on b7, but Black attacks your queen with the bishop on f6. Look for the black piece you can pin to the king.
rot.pin.pratica.pecaPresa.err.h4d4: The queen captures the pawn on d4, but the bishop on e5 recaptures. Look for the black piece you can pin to the king.
rot.pin.pratica.pecaPresa.err.h4h7: The queen captures the pawn with check, but the king recaptures. Look for the black piece you can pin to the king.
rot.pin.pratica.relativa.enunciado: Now with Black, in a Caro-Kann game. The pawn on b4 attacks your queen. Before retreating, see what stands behind the pawn on a3. Play as Black and find the best move.
rot.pin.pratica.relativa.fim: On b4 the bishop captured the pawn. The pawn on a3 recaptured and left the a-file, and your queen captured the rook on a1.
rot.pin.pratica.relativa.err.recuo: The queen gets out of the attack, but you miss a gain of material. Before retreating, see what stands behind the pawn on a3.
rot.pin.pratica.relativa.err.a5b5: The queen captures the bishop on b5, but the knight on c3 recaptures. See what stands behind the pawn on a3.
rot.pin.pratica.relativa.err.a5b4: The queen captures the pawn on b4, but the pawn on a3 recaptures. See what happens if the pawn on a3 leaves the a-file.
rot.pin.pratica.relativa.err.a5a3: The queen captures the pawn on a3, but the bishop on c1 recaptures. See what happens if the pawn on a3 leaves the a-file.
rot.pin.pratica.relativa.err2.a5b4: The queen captures the pawn with check, but the prize was the rook on a1: you are left with two pawns for a bishop. See what was left unprotected on the a-file.
